name: Chuanqiandian Cluster Miao
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Wang Fushi. 1985. Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language] (Minzu chubanshe) — standard Chinese sketch covering the Chuanqiandian dialect's phonology; no online copy found

sources.citation: Ratliff, Martha. 2010. Hmong-Mien language history. Pacific Linguistics 613. Canberra.
sources.note: Family-level only: p.199 (sec.4.2.1) Hmong-Mien nominal prefixes 'are unstressed, and in some languages they may harmonize with the nouns to which they are attached (Chen 1993)'; p.28 iambic rhythm remark concerns Mien/Mun. Nothing specific to Dananshan/CQD.

sources.citation: Mortensen, David R. 2006. Logical and substantive scales in phonology. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley (eScholarship qt0sp1b9w8).
sources.note: Sec.3.2.1 treats Dananshan Hmong tone sandhi (from Wang 1985) with no stress remark; pp.246-247 'like Jingpho, Hmong has (according to the available evidence) iambic stress and right-headed prosodic constituents' refers to Mong Leng (US, glottocode hmon1264/hnj), and p.197 'iambs, with an unstressed prefix' refers to A-Hmao — neither is chua1256.

sources.citation: Luo Xinggui 罗兴贵 & Yang Yadong 杨亚东. 2016 [1st ed. 2004]. 现代苗语概论：西部方言 Xiandai Miaoyu gailun: xibu fangyan. Guiyang: Guizhou minzu chubanshe (ISBN 978-7-5412-1853-8). Online full-text edition, yuncunzhai.com book 236526 (Dananshan-based standard Western Miao)
sources.note: Chapters on 声母, 韵母, 声调 (8 tones, ten sandhi rules), word formation and nouns fetched sources and searched: no occurrence of 重音/轻声/轻读/重读/弱化. Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: de Sousa, Hilário. 2015 (draft 2014). The Far Southern Sinitic languages as part of Mainland Southeast Asia.
sources.note: Uses Dananshan Hmong (Wang 1985) as a comparison language for segmental features; nothing on Hmong stress.

sources.citation: Kim, Won Ho. 2011. Thematic groupings in Magpie Miao narrative. MA thesis, University of North Dakota (Agongzhai village; CQD orthography).
sources.note: Discourse study; only an orthography note ('the eight tones are represented by means of a final consonant'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Li Yunbing 李雲兵. 2003. 苗瑤語聲調問題 [Issues of tone in Hmong-Mien]. Language and Linguistics 4.4: 683-712.
sources.note: Historical tonology (tone splits, mergers, prefix loss + sandhi) with CQD data (Xinshao, Mile); no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Chinese Wikipedia, 苗语川黔滇次方言 (raw wikitext; Dananshan phonology after Wang 1985)
sources.note: Initials, rhymes, tones, sandhi; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wang Fushi 王辅世 (ed.). 1985. 苗语简志 Miaoyu jianzhi [A sketch of the Miao language]. Beijing: Minzu chubanshe. 2+203 pp. (Dananshan 大南山 = Chuanqiandian representative point, phonology pp.16-23; general phonology pp.3-6)
sources.note: Nothing for Dananshan: initials, rhymes, 8 tones (43 31 55 21 44 33 13 24) and detailed tone-sandhi rules only; no 重音/轻声/轻读 anywhere in the Dananshan section or the general sections (the book's only 轻声 remark, p.12, concerns Layiping = Western Xong prefixes). Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Miao Language Team 1962, 'A brief description of the Miao language', translated in Purnell, Herbert C. (ed.) 1972, Miao and Yao linguistic studies (Cornell SEAP Data Paper 88), Chuanqiandian section with Xianjin/Dananshan phonology
sources.note: 'stress'/'accent' do not occur; prefixes discussed only for vowel harmony (Huishui) and tone sandhi ('the preceding syllable affects the following syllable'). Silent.

sources.citation: Graham, David Crockett. 1954. Songs and stories of the Ch'uan Miao. Smithsonian Miscellaneous Collections 123 (Ch'uan Miao = Sichuan Hmong, CQD first vernacular).
sources.note: pp.9-10 'Grammar and pronunciation': monosyllabic, nine tones; the 'little aspirate' is 'pronounced with a strong emphasis' (a phonation remark, not word stress). No stress statement.

sources.citation: Johnson, Michael & David Strecker. 2020. An overview of Hmong Sha (West Hmongic, Guangnan): phonology and lexicon. Unpublished manuscript.
